cells.tense: You're here in it right now, able to begin a session with no fixed idea of where it's headed.
cells.ask: follow one spark that hasn't earned its keep yet and see what it turns into
cells.core:
The practice you keep is alive because you sit down without needing the outcome pre-decided. You pick up the same work as if you'd never done it, and the freshness is what makes the repetition hold. That open start is available to you in almost any hour you choose to give it. Let it feed the one thing you'd try purely because it interests you, with nothing to show for it yet.

What keeps it going is that you don't treat the first spark as a debt to be justified. You begin, you stay, you let the direction show up later. This is the balance that nothing else has to be sacrificed for. The beginner's stance is already yours, and it stays yours as long as you keep offering it to the work in front of you.
cells.sheetLine: You begin without already knowing, and that's what keeps the practice fresh.
cells.verb: letting something new spark before you know where it's going
cells.place: in the daily work of getting better at one thing

cells.tense: You're already working toward some future version of this, trying to nail it down before it arrives.
cells.ask: look at what's actually in front of you once, then leave it exactly where it is
cells.core:
At its healthiest, this is sitting down with the tools you have and letting the session teach you what it's for. You show up, you pay attention, and the next move reveals itself in its own time. That's the version of practice that doesn't cost you anything to keep.

The pressure to be ready is what's crowding it out. Every session turns into a bid for a moment that hasn't happened, and the work gets heavier without getting truer. Seeing clearly — one plain look at what's here — is what's being asked for. It's an offer, and it's yours to take or leave.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a starting line that's already behind you.
cells.ask: let one person's presence reach you, not to fix the work but to sit with you in it
cells.core:
The work at its steady best is a small light you keep lit by returning — not by force, but by showing up. The tools stay where you left them, the door stays open, and the next beginning is a thing you can take.

The practice sits there and nothing catches. You can still put in the hours, but the hours don't land anywhere, and the room you're working in has gone quiet in a way that no amount of trying has shifted. What's thin isn't effort. It's the felt connection that used to make the work matter. That connection comes back sideways, through someone whose presence you let in. Let it deepen rather than resolve.
cells.sheetLine: The work is still there, but you can't feel why it matters.

cells.tense: Something in the practice is already moving, and you're describing it as if it moved itself.
cells.ask: catch one decision to begin and say it's yours, once, out loud
cells.core:
In its healthy shape, this is a person who sits down at the same hour and starts, and knows that starting is a choice they keep making. The light is small and steady because someone keeps lighting it. The practice is an ordinary, tended thing, and the tending is the point.

What's running underneath is the beginning itself — the spark that shows up in the work before it has a shape. You keep attributing it to the routine or the schedule. But you're the one who decides to start again, and that decision is already happening. Say it plainly, once, and you'll have it back.
cells.sheetLine: You keep beginning, and the beginning is yours to claim.
